identity.title: Pupils and eye movements: miosis with hypoventilation (opioid), ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus with ataxia (Wernicke), gaze deviation

technique.how: Measure pupil size and reactivity in dim light, count respiratory rate for a full minute. Test horizontal and vertical pursuit and check for nystagmus, lateral rectus (VI) palsy or conjugate gaze palsy; note any forced gaze deviation at rest. Then test gait or heel-shin for ataxia and screen mental state and short-term recall.
technique.prerequisites: Pen light; ability to open the eyelids; record any recent opioid, sedative or eye-drop exposure and prior ocular surgery.

interpretation.positive_finding: Pinpoint pupils with respiratory rate <=12 in an unresponsive patient points to opioid toxidrome and justifies naloxone. Nystagmus, VI palsy or gaze palsy plus ataxia or confusion in a malnourished or alcohol-using patient meets Caine criteria for Wernicke's and mandates immediate IV thiamine; forced conjugate gaze deviation suggests stroke or ongoing seizure.
interpretation.negative_finding: Normal pupils do not exclude opioid effect after mixed ingestions or hypoxia. The full Wernicke triad was documented in only 16% of necropsy-proven cases, so absence of eye signs must not withhold thiamine in at-risk patients.
interpretation.pitfalls: Miosis also follows pontine stroke, clonidine, organophosphates and cholinergic eye drops; mydriasis after hypoxic arrest can mask opioid miosis. Wernicke's without alcohol (bariatric surgery, hyperemesis, cancer) presents atypically; eye signs are frequently missed on record review.
interpretation.changes_what: Miosis + hypoventilation: give naloxone and support ventilation. Eye-movement signs + ataxia/confusion: IV thiamine now, before glucose. Gaze deviation: stroke pathway or EEG.

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: classic Wernicke triad (oculomotor abnormality + cerebellar ataxia + altered mental state) all documented antemortem, for necropsy-proven Wernicke-Korsakoff
estimates.population: 131 cases of Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome diagnosed at necropsy, Western Australia, retrospective review of clinical records (80% undiagnosed in life)
estimates.quote: only 16% had the classical clinical triad and 19% had no documented clinical signs

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: Caine operational criteria (2 of 4: dietary deficiency, eye signs, cerebellar dysfunction, altered mental state/memory impairment) for neuropathologically confirmed Wernicke's encephalopathy co-occurring with hepatic encephalopathy
estimates.population: 106 alcoholics screened from a large necropsy sample; criteria applied retrospectively to patient records by 3 independent raters; subgroup with Wernicke's plus hepatic encephalopathy
estimates.quote: Wernicke's encephalopathy was underrecognized only when occurring with hepatic encephalopathy (50% sensitivity)

sources.citation: Harper CG, Giles M, Finlay-Jones R. Clinical signs in the Wernicke-Korsakoff complex: a retrospective analysis of 131 cases diagnosed at necropsy. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 1986;49(4):341-345.

Caine D, Halliday GM, Kril JJ, Harper CG. Operational criteria for the classification of chronic alcoholics: identification of Wernicke's encephalopathy. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 1997;62(1):51-60.
Galvin R, Bråthen G, Ivashynka A, Hillbom M, Tanasescu R, Leone MA. EFNS guidelines for diagnosis, therapy and prevention of Wernicke encephalopathy. Eur J Neurol. 2010;17(12):1408-1418.
Hoffman JR, Schriger DL, Luo JS. The empiric use of naloxone in patients with altered mental status: a reappraisal. Ann Emerg Med. 1991;20(3):246-252.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Never withhold thiamine or naloxone because the eye or pupil findings are absent; both treatments are low-risk and the signs are insensitive.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Hypoventilation with miosis needs airway support and naloxone now; new gaze deviation or ophthalmoplegia with headache or focal deficits needs urgent neuroimaging.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Caine 1997 reports 100% between-rater agreement for diagnostic classification using the criteria on records, quote 'within and between rater reliability for diagnostic classification using the criteria retrospectively on patient records was 100% for three independent raters' (Abstract), despite variability for individual signs.

extraction_notes: Both Wernicke estimates are COMPOSITE criteria sensitivities from necropsy series (case-only design, so no specificity or prevalence); individual sign accuracy (eye signs alone) is in the full texts of PMIDs 3701343 and 9010400, which are abstract-only in PMC and inaccessible here. Opioid component: Hoffman 1991 (PMID 1996818, n=730 AMS patients given naloxone) states that respirations <=12 or any of the three findings (respirations <=12, miotic pupils, circumstantial evidence) were 'highly sensitive in predicting response to naloxone' but the abstract gives no sensitivity figure for miosis alone, so no estimate entered; full text not in PMC. Search 'opioid overdose miosis respiratory rate naloxone response sensitivity' returned nothing. Gaze deviation for stroke/seizure: no diagnostic-accuracy source searched within budget; described from guideline-level teaching only. EFNS guideline (PMID 20642790) recommends Caine 2-of-4 criteria in alcoholics (Level B). Status partially_quantified (sensitivity only, composites).
